## 1) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive, so the block can be bypassed

Affected:
- app/models/blocked_email.rb:11-19
- db/migrate/20130724201552_create_blocked_emails.rb:4,10

Explanation:
`BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` is an exact, case-sensitive match on PostgreSQL. If `bad@spammers.org` is blocked, signing up as `Bad@Spammers.org` gets through. Nothing in this diff normalizes the email before storing or comparing it. The model's `uniqueness: true` and the unique index are also case-sensitive, so the same address can be stored twice with different casing.

Fix: downcase the email when saving it and when looking it up, or compare with `lower(email)`.

Proposed fix:
~~~ruby
before_validation { self.email = email.try(:downcase) }

def self.should_block?(email)
  record = BlockedEmail.where(email: email.to_s.downcase).first
  ...
end
~~~

## 2) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Validation has a write side effect, and the counter update can lose increments

Affected:
- app/models/blocked_email.rb:11-19
- lib/validators/email_validator.rb:13-15

Explanation:
`should_block?` runs inside a model validation, but it writes to the database. Every `valid?` / `save` attempt increments `match_count` and touches `last_match_at`. This includes repeated validation of the same record in one request and any availability-check endpoint that calls `valid?`. The statistics will therefore be inflated and do not reflect actual blocked signups.

The increment is also a read-modify-write (`match_count += 1; save`). Concurrent requests will lose updates.

Fix:
- Increment atomically in SQL.
- Consider separating the "check" from the "record a match" step.

Proposed fix:
~~~ruby
def self.should_block?(email)
  record = BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first
  if record
    BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all(["match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?", Time.zone.now])
  end
  record && record.action_type == actions[:block]
end
~~~

## 3) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Security
Title: Domain whitelist/blacklist regex is unanchored and treats the setting as a raw regex

Affected:
- lib/validators/email_validator.rb:18-22

Explanation:
This code was moved here unchanged, but it now lives in a new validator, so it is worth fixing. The regex `@(example\.com)` is not anchored at the end of the string, which causes two problems:
- **Whitelist bypass:** with `example.com` whitelisted, `x@example.com.attacker.org` passes.
- **Blacklist false positive:** with `spam.com` blacklisted, `x@spam.com.au` is rejected.

In addition, only `.` is escaped. Any other regex metacharacter in the setting is interpreted as regex syntax.

Fix: split the setting on `|`, escape each domain with `Regexp.escape`, and anchor the pattern with `\z`.

Proposed fix:
~~~ruby
def email_in_restriction_setting?(setting, value)
  domains = setting.split('|').map { |d| Regexp.escape(d.strip) }.join('|')
  value =~ Regexp.new("@(#{domains})\\z", true)
end
~~~

## 4) Severity: LOW | Type: Bug
Title: Any server-side email error permanently marks the email as "invalid" in the form

Affected:
- app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/create_account_controller.js:69-74
- app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/create_account_controller.js:274-276

Explanation:
The client adds the email to `rejectedEmails` whenever `result.errors.email` is present. That includes errors that have nothing to do with blocking, such as "has already been taken" or a transient domain-setting error. From then on the field shows the generic `user.email.invalid` message instead of the real reason.

There are two further problems:
- `result.values.email` comes from the server's attributes. If the server normalizes the email (for example by downcasing it), it will not match what the user typed in `accountEmail`, so the client check never triggers.
- `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` is declared on the class prototype, so the array is shared across controller instances.

Fix:
- Show the actual server error message rather than a generic "invalid".
- Initialize the array in `init`.

Proposed fix:
~~~js
init: function() {
  this._super();
  this.set('rejectedEmails', Em.A([]));
},
~~~

## 5) Severity: LOW | Type: Test
Title: Moved whitelist/blacklist logic has no tests in the new validator spec

Affected:
- spec/components/validators/email_validator_spec.rb:1-23

Explanation:
The spec only covers the blocked-email branch, and it does so with stubs. The domain whitelist/blacklist logic moved out of `User` into `EmailValidator` but has no coverage here. The spec also does not check that the blocked check is skipped when a domain error was already added.

Fix: add cases that stub `SiteSetting.email_domains_whitelist` and `SiteSetting.email_domains_blacklist`, and assert that `should_block?` is not called when a domain error already exists.

Proposed fix:
~~~ruby
it "adds an error when domain not in whitelist" do
  SiteSetting.stubs(:email_domains_whitelist).returns("example.com")
  BlockedEmail.expects(:should_block?).never
  validate
  record.errors[:email].should be_present
end
~~~
